text:
Anika (Design): Quick design review 1 updated API Keys modal screens uploaded. Main friction: rotate flow looks destructive. Users might think rotating deletes all keys or deletes the service. Thoughts?

Josh (PM): Agree. Also noticed the primary action ordering 1 Rotate is the left-most button in the modal, which is risky. Primary should be the safe action or we should highlight the destructive nature more. :eyes:

Mara (Frontend): Implementation note 1 backend returns the new secret only once on rotate. We need copy that forces users to copy/save immediately. Current mock says 'New key created' but doesn't tell them it's one-time. Suggested inline copy: "This is the only time you'll see the new key 1 copy it now. We won't be able to show it again."

Leo (Security): Also add a permissions/usage warning for high-impact keys. If a key has service integrations or >100k tokens in 30d, require an explicit confirmation (checkbox + type-to-confirm). Example: checkbox: "I understand this will stop requests using the old key." and typed confirmation: `ROTATE` for very high-impact keys.

Anika (Design): Good call. Proposed microcopy for the modal header: "Rotate API key" and subcopy: "This will create a new credential and immediately revoke the previous key. You will only see the new key once." For the primary CTA label I propose: "Rotate and copy key" (primary, accent color) and secondary: "Cancel" (neutral). That keeps intent clear.

Emily (Accessibility): Nits: ensure focus order: close button -> modal title -> subcopy -> first form control -> primary CTA. Use `aria-describedby` for the subcopy so screen readers read the warning first. For the one-time secret exposure use `aria-live="assertive"` on the copy box with a short announcement: "New key revealed. This is the only time it will be shown." Also ensure keyboard users can get to the copy button without a mouse.

Mara (Frontend): Dev nit 1 we currently present the secret in a `<pre>` with a copy button. I'll add `role="status" aria-live="polite"` to the copy confirmation toast. For the one-time reveal, `aria-live="assertive"` is probably better per Emily.

Josh (PM): Copy alternatives for the destructive warning 1 A/B test these two lines: 1) "Rotating will immediately revoke the existing key." 2) "A new key will be issued; the previous key will stop working immediately." Which reads clearer? My gut says #2 is friendlier.

Anika (Design): I prefer #2 as well. Less legal-sounding. Will update Figma and add hover tooltips on the key-list row explaining scopes and recent activity. Also adding an empty-state variant: "You don't have any API keys yet 1 create a key to get started." CTA: "Create API key" (primary). Keep empty guidance concise with a link to docs.

Leo (Security): One more policy ask 1 show last used timestamp and IP/country on each key row, and add a small warning icon if key hasn't been rotated in >180 days. Clicking the icon should open a small modal with risk summary + suggested action.

Emily (Accessibility): Extra a11y check: when revoking a key, we should trap focus in the confirm modal and move focus to the heading on open. When the action completes, announce success with an `aria-live` region: "Key revoked". For revertible actions (rotate), provide a clear undo path in the UI or call out that undo is not possible.

Mara (Frontend): For revoke vs rotate CTA placement 1 let's make destructive actions always the rightmost red button to reduce accidental clicks. Current modals vary. I'll standardize the component.

Anika (Design): I'll update the mocks to: (1) standardized CTA ordering, (2) explicit one-time-key copy affordance, (3) optional typed-confirm for high-impact keys, and (4) accessible live-region wording. Posting new frames in 30m.

Josh (PM): Sweet. After deploy-preview goes up let's run a quick 15-min hallway test with 3 engineers + 1 designer + 1 accessibility reviewer. Goal: validate focus order, copy clarity, and accidental-rotate risk. Quick winners: change CTA label to "Rotate and copy key", add one-time copy banner, and move destructive button to the right. :thumbsup:

Anika (Design): Thanks all 1 I'll push the changes and ping when the new frames are live.

Mara (Frontend): I'll grab the preview and wire up the live-region behaviors. Will ping if any API changes needed for confirmation/typed input.

Leo (Security): I'll draft the typed-confirm thresholds and share in this thread.

Emily (Accessibility): I'll run a screen-reader pass on the preview ASAP. If I spot anything blocking I'll drop notes here.

Anika (Design): :rocket:
